title: End-of-day chairs up: lift a preschool chair, turn it over and set it seat down, legs up, on the table
instruction: Put the child's chair up on the table: lift it from the floor with both hands, turn it over and set it down gently, seat down with its legs up, the seat's back edge on the table's near edge or up to 3 cm past it, without dropping it, knocking the table with it or sliding it along the top. Then let go and move your hands away.
context: At the end of the school day the chairs go up on the tables so the floor can be swept and mopped; almost everyone has done it, and preschool staff and school janitors do it every day with child-sized chairs and low tables. The chair is lifted by the sides of its seat, turned over and lowered seat down onto the top, its back hanging over the near edge. What goes wrong: a leg or the back knocks the table, the chair is let fall the last few centimetres, or it lands skewed and slides. The physics is the hard part: the 1.4 kg polypropylene shell is smooth, and its centre of mass sits 5 cm behind the seat's middle, so a grip off that line lets it swing; the half-turn must clear a top 30.5 cm high with a chair 50.8 cm tall, and the landing must stay under 0.5 m/s, fall no more than 12 mm and slide less than 3 cm. Both hands are needed for the lift and the turn. A picture cannot answer it: the score reads the whole path (drops, knocks, slide) as well as the end.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a bench whose top stands for the classroom floor. Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the floor. CHAIR: Flash Furniture Whitney stackable preschool chair, model YU-YCX-003 (dealer listings of the 2-pack: webstaurantstore.com 354CX003GRN, quill.com 2YUYCX003BLUE, and Flash's own product page 2-YU-YCX-003-RED-GG): one moulded polypropylene shell with four splayed legs from the seat's corners, no metal; 12.5 in wide, 14 in deep, 20 in high (31.8 x 35.6 x 50.8 cm; Flash Furniture's product sheet and staples.com); seat 10 x 10 in (25.4 cm square) at 10.75 in (27.3 cm) high; back 11 in (27.9 cm) wide, rising from the seat's rear edge. The chair stands on the floor with its seat centre at (10, 0), facing the arms. Mass 1.4 kg, an estimate: no per-chair mass is published; the 2-pack is listed at 6 lb (quill.com, staples.com) in a 10 lb carton (webstaurantstore.com), so about 3 lb (1.4 kg) a chair. Also estimates: shell 12 mm, legs 25 mm across. In the scene the seat and back are flat plates and the legs straight tubes from the seat's corners; the real shell's dished seat, edge band and hand hole between seat and back are not modelled, and the back plate is 24.7 cm high from the seat's underside (published back 10.5 in, 26.7 cm, measured into the edge band). TABLE: Community Playthings Woodcrest rectangular table C241 as a 12 in (30.5 cm) high table, the lowest of the maker's 12 to 20 in heights (communityplaythings.com), chosen so the arms reach it: solid maple top 30 x 22 in (76.2 x 55.9 cm), 1 1/8 in thick, no apron. Its long side is across the arms, its near edge at x = 29.8, centred on y = 0, its top face 30.5 cm above the floor. NOT CONFIRMED by the maker: the leg section (45 mm used). Nothing else is on the table. Product names are for identification only and are trademarks of their owners. The arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Photo, ruler, 240 fps film. 0.25: both hands hold it 8 cm up, or it rests on top. 0.5: also seat down within 30 deg. 0.75: on top within 5 deg, let go, still 1 s. 1.0: back edge 0-3 cm past edge, fingertips 3 cm and arm links 5 cm off, still 2 s. 0: lifted or turned without both hands in contact from lift-off until the seat is within 35 deg of down (both pads of each hand within 2 mm of the chair; a hand beside it does not count), or turned over on the floor (seat past 145 deg from down while any part is within 5 mm of the floor), falls 12 mm, lands at 0.5 m/s, leg, back or seat over 30 deg from down, or any part touching a table leg, hits table (the back may touch the near face only if the seat is down and it arrives under 0.5 m/s), slid 3 cm on top.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; the table is fixed and the bench top is the floor. The chair is plates and tubes at the maker's sizes, without its dished seat, edge band or hand hole; its 1.4 kg mass (a 6 lb 2-pack), 12 mm shell and 25 mm legs are estimates. Pads pinch the seat plate, then the back plate, at 35 N per finger, set friction. The demo reads the chair's pose and the fingertips. Falls, landing speed and touches are read at every physics step (240 Hz), each leg along its length; no force is read.
